key_insight: MARTINI-3 coarse-grained clay parameters can predict how phyllosilicate clays compatibilize immiscible polymer blends by tuning interfacial structure and polarity.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster large-scale simulation and design of clay-based polymer nanocomposites with improved blend compatibility, especially for TPS-PE systems.
method: Derived initial clay surface interactions from hydration free energies using Lifshitz theory and experimental surface tension data.
Fine-tuned MARTINI-3 phyllosilicate parameters against all-atom MD of thermoplastic starch–clay composites.
Applied the CG model to simulate C12TAB-modified montmorillonite in TPS-PE blends and quantify interfacial tension reduction.
evidence_signal: The CG model matched all-atom and experimental benchmarks, and captured TPS-PE interfacial tension dropping from 45 mN/m to 13.06 mN/m with amphiphilic clay.
watch_item: Transferability may depend on how well the chosen clay functionalization and polymer chemistry match the calibrated systems.
paper_title: Characterization and Quantification of Immiscible Polymer Blend Compatibilization by Phyllosilicate Clays
